title: Bridging Semantics and Utilities: A Controllable and Scalable Market Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2611.18613v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models(LLMs) have recently been used to construct generative agents for financial market simulation. Existing approaches typically prompt each agent separately with public market information and a private investor profile, and ask the model to directly generate trading actions. In this agent-wise design, the model repeatedly interprets information shared across the population, while individual behavior is controlled through textual descriptions of investor preferences and traits. This creates two structural difficulties: continuous traits such as risk sensitivity do not reliably induce ordered behavioral changes, and repeatedly processing the same public information causes inference costs to grow with the number of agents. We propose \textbf{SUM}, a Semantic-Utility Model that separates cohort-level semantic perception from agent-level utility-based decision-making. translated_title: 连接语义与效用：一种可控且可扩展的市场模拟
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）近来被用于构建面向金融市场模拟的生成式智能体。现有方法通常为每个智能体单独提供公共市场信息和私人投资者画像作为提示，并要求模型直接生成交易行为。在这种逐个智能体的设计中，模型反复解读群体共享的信息，而个体行为则通过投资者偏好与特质的文本描述来控制。这带来了两个结构性难题：诸如风险敏感性等连续特质无法可靠地引发有序的行为变化，且反复处理相同的公共信息导致推理成本随智能体数量增长。我们提出了SUM（语义-效用模型），将群体层面的语义感知与智能体层面的基于效用的决策制定相分离。语言模型为……解读公共市场信息（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出SUM语义-效用模型，通过将群体级语义感知与个体级基于效用的决策相分离，解决了现有LLM金融市场中行为控制不可靠和推理成本随智能体数量增长两大问题，实现了可控且可扩展的市场模拟。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SUM, a Semantic-Utility Model that separates cohort-level semantic perception from agent-level utility-based decision-making, addressing unreliable behavior control and scaling inference costs in LLM-based market simulation to achieve controllable and scalable market simulation.
